SAME STRUCTURE AS THE OTHER OLYMPIAD YEARS -- problem1..problem6 against the paper's Problems 1 to 6, resp exactly 0-7, three problems per day -- with one difference in how the text was obtained. The 2016 PDF's text layer is a symbol font that extracts as mojibake (1,808 symbol characters against 641 ASCII letters, where the other years run the other way), so it was rendered at 150 dpi and transcribed from the images. That makes this the only year in the batch with correct superscripts and subscripts. The transcription is manual and unverified character by character, which no numeric route could check either way.

THE CODEBOOK SHIPPED WITH THE DATA IS THE WHOLE SOURCE, and the processing script renames nothing, so the live codes SC1-SC10 are the codebook's own. Re-reading codebook.txt gives exactly ten SC items matching the live set, and every shipped item_text matches the codebook string with the documented "I " prefix -- the only difference being the first letter's case, which the prefix requires. The five anchors are the codebook's, and the live levels are exactly 1-5 with no 0, consistent with the script dropping unanswered items. Item set matches at 10.

THE SCRIPT WAS RE-RUN OVER THE DEPOSIT'S THREE CSVs, which is the only safe route for a row_number() code assigned over an rbind, and it reproduces exactly: 65,291 rows against the live 65,291, 339 items, 617 participants. The blocks come out contiguous -- 1-93, 94-191, 192-339 for the 95-, 100- and 150-trial studies. THE RE-RUN ALSO ESTABLISHED AN OFF-BY-ONE IN THE SOURCE READ, from the files' own shape rather than from inference: choice_95.csv has 95 header names and 96 fields per data row, because the subject label column is unnamed, so read_csv assigns 'Choice_1' to the subject label and every trial shifts one place, with the last field of each row dropped unnamed. The same holds for the 100- and 150-trial files. That is why the studies contribute 93, 98 and 148 items rather than 95, 100 and 150. The shipped item_text reports the true trial number, not the column number. The deck coding is quoted from the paper and matches the live levels 1-4 exactly. What no route establishes is any administered wording -- the task is a screen of four decks with the same action every trial, so item_text is a bracketed description.
